data.summary: Decision 126 rules that a supplied FaultPlan is conditional on execution reaching its fault-delivery point. An earlier authority denial records the denial and actual prefix but not the unreached fault. A contrary hardware trace is a model/profile validation discrepancy, while an offered plan may be retained only in a separate diagnostic channel. The provisional M2 behavior is therefore correct.

Decision 127 rules that obligation-ledger transformations are indexed by exact operation outcomes and their protocol-declared linearization points, independently of memory visibility. Grass must not infer fault behavior from committed byte counts or delta kind. A missing fault rule rejects fail-closed, so faultWithUndeclaredLedgerEffect remains correct until an outcome-indexed protocol proof admits that combination.

Ruling adopted: process assertions are indexed by an explicit world agreement. ProcessPlan declares its per-edge Message family before channel contracts; topology plus Message defines LogicalProcessNetworkCore, and contracts bind to the canonical agreement for that complete world. LogicalProcessNetwork plan remains the public abbreviation. No opaque topology-level escrow carrier is introduced.

data.summary: Adversarial review of the candidate successor coordination design. The draft addresses the observed single-ref/single-lock contention with per-agent remote streams and one host-coordinator publisher per physical box; agents otherwise use immutable local outboxes and cached lock-free reads. It separately defines non-obligating friction reports routed to the design steward, and durable topic/subscription/audience-snapshot broadcasts with bounded acknowledgement semantics. The candidate explicitly preserves V1 until an epoch migration and fixtures succeed.

Ruling adopted and documented as decision 131. ChannelContract keeps authored assertions, checkable footprint-locality witnesses, and send/receive obligations over an explicit ChannelSteps parameter. Stability, framing, and ReceiverPre/Escrow separability are derived; conservation and affine resolution belong to the ledger; exhaustive resolution and exact transfer belong to transition-family realization. The seven undeclared opaque promise fields are removed without weakening their intended laws.
